A bride served the Prophet soaked dates; Sauda soaked dates in a skin till worn out; his family never had their fill of wheat bread with meat three days running.
When Abu Talha and Um Sulaim sent the hungry Prophet barley loaves, he came with his companions and blessed the bread, and seventy or eighty men ate their fill.
Deeds are rewarded by intentions: emigration for Allah and His Apostle counts as such, while emigration for worldly gain or to marry a woman counts only for that.
Repenting for staying behind from Tabuk, Ka'b bin Malik offered all his property for Allah and His Apostle, but the Prophet told him to keep some, as that was better.
When Aisha and Hafsa agreed to say he smelled of Maghafir, the Prophet swore off the honey he drank at Zainab's, and verses 66.1-4 were revealed.
A vow neither hastens nor delays anything Allah has decreed, only drawing out a miser's wealth; after the best generations will come people who vow without fulfilling and testify unasked.
A vow to obey Allah must be kept, one to disobey Him not; Umar was told to fulfil a pre-Islamic I'tikaf vow; vows of the dead are fulfilled for them.
The Prophet rejected self-torment, cut ropes leading men round the Ka'bah, and let Abu Israil keep only his vow's fast; Ibn Umar cited the ban on fasting Eid.
When an arrow killed the slave Mid'am, the Prophet swore the sheet he stole from Khaibar's booty was burning on him, and called returned shoe straps straps of fire.
Lice-troubled Ka'b could expiate by fasting, charity or sacrifice; for intercourse while fasting in Ramadan, a man unable to free a slave, fast or feed sixty fed his family.
The Prophet's Sa' was a later Mudd and a third; Ibn Umar paid Zakat al-Fitr and oath expiations by the Prophet's Mudd; the Prophet asked Allah to bless Medina's measures.
Freeing a Muslim slave saves each of the freer's limbs from the Fire; the Prophet sold a Mudabbar slave, a man's only property; the Wala goes to the freer.
The Prophet swore not to give the Ash'ariyin mounts, then gave them camels, saying Allah provided them and that, Allah willing, he expiates an oath when he finds something better.
Solomon forgot to say 'If Allah will' when hoping ninety wives would bear warriors, so only one bore, a half-boy; had he said it, he would have got his wish.
Abu Musa told a man who swore off chicken how the Prophet broke an oath for something better and expiated; Abdur-Rahman was told likewise, and not to seek rule.
When Jabir lay unconscious the Prophet poured his ablution water over him; Jabir asked how to distribute his property, and the Prophet did not reply until the inheritance verses came.
Beware of suspicion, the worst of false tales; do not seek faults, spy, hate or desert one another, but be brothers, O Allah's slaves.
The prophets' property is not inherited but spent in charity, after the family's provision, as Abu Bakr told Fatima and Al-Abbas, Umar told Ali and Abbas, and Aisha the wives.
The Prophet pays the debts of believers who die leaving nothing, while any property goes to the heirs: the prescribed shares first, then the remainder to the closest male relative.
Near death with one daughter as heir, Sa'd was allowed to give a third in charity, though even that is much, as heirs are better left rich than poor.
A daughter takes half, a son's daughter a sixth, a sister the rest; shares come first, then the closest male; parents and spouses have fixed portions; Emigrant-Ansar brotherhood inheritance ended.
After a Li'an case the child went to the wife alone, and over Zam'a's slave girl's son the Prophet ruled that the boy belongs to the bed's owner.
The Wala goes to the one who pays and frees, as with Barira, who then left her husband; it may not be sold or given; Muslims freed none as Sa'iba.
A sister's son belongs to her people; a man's property goes to his heirs, his debts and dependants to the Prophet; Muslims and disbelievers do not inherit from each other.
Zam'a's slave girl's disputed son went to the bed's owner, Sauda screening herself; knowingly claiming another man as father forbids Paradise; whoever denies his father is charged with disbelief.
A wolf took one of two women's sons; David gave the boy to the elder, but Solomon, offering to cut him in two, gave him to the younger, who objected.
The Prophet was delighted when Mujazziz, seeing only the uncovered feet of Zaid and Usama, said these feet belong to each other.
An adulterer, a drinker, a thief and a robber watched by people are not believers while committing these acts.
The Prophet had drinkers beaten with palm stalks, shoes, hands and garments, forbidding cursing them; Abu Bakr gave forty lashes, Umar forty then eighty; Ali said none were fixed.
An adulterer is not a believer while committing illegal intercourse, nor a thief while stealing.
Allah curses the thief whose hand is cut for an egg or a rope; Al-A'mash says people took these as an iron helmet and a rope worth dirhams.
Taking a pledge against polytheism, theft and illegal intercourse, the Prophet said a legal punishment for such a sin expiates it, while one Allah screens is left to His will.
In the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet declared blood, property and honour as sacred as that day, town and month, and warned against reverting to disbelief by killing one another.
The Prophet chose the easier of two options unless it was sinful, and never took revenge for himself, only for Allah's sake when His limits were transgressed.
When Usama interceded for a Makhzumi woman thief, the Prophet said earlier nations perished by punishing the weak and sparing the noble, and swore he would cut even Fatima's hand.
A thief's hand is cut for a quarter dinar or more, not for less than a shield's price, as the Prophet did for a shield worth three dirhams.
A woman whose hand the Prophet cut repented sincerely; a legal punishment expiates and purifies the sins named in the pledge, and a repentant thief's witness is accepted.
Ukl men cured by camels' milk and urine turned renegades, killed the shepherd, took the camels; their hands and feet were cut, eyes branded, and they were left to die.
Allah will shade seven on Resurrection Day, including one refusing a noble woman's call to illegal intercourse; the Prophet guarantees Paradise to whoever guards his tongue and private parts.
Among the Hour's signs: religious knowledge taken away, ignorance spreading, drinking and open illegal intercourse common, and women so many that fifty have one man to look after them.
